subject: Post-call recap: NovaHealth infra SLOs, isolation & scaling
messages:
From: Priyom Das <priyom@redwood.com>
To: Alex Johnson <alex.j@novahealth.ai>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 1 Jun 2027 14:03:00 -0700
Subject: Post-call recap: NovaHealth infra SLOs, isolation & scaling

Alex — thanks again for a focused discussion earlier. Below is a short recap to make sure we’re aligned and to capture next steps. If I missed anything, please flag.

Summary of pain points you raised
- Production latency spikes at 95th/99th under peak (current 95th ~600ms on short prompts; up to multiple seconds for long-context ops).
- Concern about PHI isolation: single-tenant guarantees, no cross-tenant inference, and strict KMS + audit requirements.
- Unpredictable batch windows for nightly model tuning/training that needs short-term extra capacity.
- Cost visibility and predictable per-request economics for forecast and procurement.

Goals (what success looks like for NovaHealth)
- Dedicated, tenant-isolated reserved pool located in US-East.
- Baseline committed capacity: 4x A100 equivalent GPUs for steady-state inference (supporting ~200–300 rps with our batching assumptions).
- Burst policy: ability to burst to 8x A100 for scheduled nightly tuning jobs (2–4 hours) and to 6x during daytime spikes for short windows.
- SLO targets: 99.9% platform uptime; P95 inference latency <= 200ms for short-context calls (where batching is effective); allow up to 1s P95 for long-context workflows while preserving throughput.
- Compliance: SOC 2 evidence, audit logs retained for 12 months, optional per-tenant KMS integration and field-level redaction for PHI.

What we propose next
1) Technical deep-dive with our infra/ops engineering to validate sizing assumptions and isolation controls (Marissa + Ben to lead). Suggested week-of 06/07.
2) Shared scoping doc: I attached a short post-call notes PDF and a capacity sketch (novahealth-capacity-draft.xlsx) — please add any missing constraints (data residency, egress rules).
3) Security intake: procurement will want SOC 2 and a short answers pack — we’ll surface that during the deep-dive.
4) Commercial path: initial 6–12 month reserved commitment with burst policy; rough timeline for procurement ~45–75 days depending on legal.

Attachments: 20270601-novahealth-postcall-notes.pdf, novahealth-capacity-draft.xlsx

Thanks — I’ll coordinate the scheduling for the technical deep-dive.

— Priyom
Priyom Das
Senior Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
priyom@redwood.com
(415) 555-0118
From: Alex Johnson <alex.j@novahealth.ai>
To: Priyom Das <priyom@redwood.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 1 Jun 2027 16:21:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Post-call recap: NovaHealth infra SLOs, isolation & scaling

Thanks Priyom — this matches our notes. A few clarifications and asks from procurement/security: 
- SOC 2 Type II report or equivalent evidence — our security team requires this for procurement.
- Audit log retention: must be configurable up to 12 months; ability to export logs on request.
- KMS: We need support for customer-managed keys (AWS KMS) and a short guide on how that impacts backup/export flows.
- Per-request data capture: we cannot store raw PHI in logs; need a pattern for field-level redaction or opt-out for logging for specific endpoints.

Timeline: we’re aiming to get the deep-dive scheduled the week of 06/07, procurement will start review right after the tech call. Can you include a rough cost/price ballpark for the 4x reserved + burst option ahead of the call? That will help the finance team prioritize.

Alex
Alex Johnson
Head of Platform Engineering, NovaHealth
alex.j@novahealth.ai
From: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>
To: Priyom Das <priyom@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 2 Jun 2027 09:08:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Post-call recap: NovaHealth infra SLOs, isolation & scaling

Priyom / Ben — thanks for capturing. Internal notes / proposed approach: 
- Initial sizing: commit-to 4x A100-equivalent. I’ll run a quick steady-state throughput calc against the NovaHealth sample traces (request shapes from the Drive link) and confirm expected rps and token cost.
- Burst design: implement policy-based autoscale window that allows controlled burst to 6x for spikes and scheduled 2–4hr nightly bursts to 8x. Burst will be metered and visible in the console.
- Isolation: recommend a single-tenant pool with network policies + VPC peering to meet residency. KMS integration is supported — engineering will prepare the KMS runbook.
- SLO draft for discussion during deep-dive: 99.9% uptime; P95 short-context <=200ms; P95 long-context <=1s; cost/throughput SLAs to be defined against committed GPUs.

Action items: 
- Ben: can you produce a short ops runbook (start/stop, cache priming, KV handling) and a failure/fallback flow for tenant pool? Attach capacity-snapshot.csv with current baseline.
- Priyom: please draft a one-page commercial ballpark (4x reserved + burst options) to share with Alex before the call.
- Marissa: I’ll set up the technical deep-dive and invite infra + security.

Attaching: capacity-snapshot.csv

Marissa Cole
Sr. Product Manager, Customer Ops
marissa@redwood.com
From: Ben Carter <ben@redwood.com>
To: Priyom Das <priyom@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 3 Jun 2027 09:12:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Post-call recap: NovaHealth infra SLOs, isolation & scaling

On Wed, Jun 2, 2027 at 09:08, Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com> wrote:
> Priyom / Ben — thanks for capturing. Internal notes / proposed approach: 
> 
> Action items: 
> - Ben: can you produce a short ops runbook (start/stop, cache priming, KV handling) and a failure/fallback flow for tenant pool? Attach capacity-snapshot.csv with current baseline.

Copying here the plan — I’ll have a draft ops runbook and the runbook checklist by EOD 06/04. High-level items I’ll cover: start/stop sequencing, cache warm/prime, KV eviction thresholds, degraded-mode fallback to lighter quantized model, monitoring hooks (console + webhook), and post-incident customer notification flow.

I’ll also add a short appendix on how we’d meter burst usage and an ops playbook for recovering from noisy neighbors despite tenant isolation (network policing + preemption policies).

Adding tech-deep-dive invite: tech-deep-dive-invite.ics (proposed 06/08 10:00 PT)

— Ben
